questions.title: Pop Two from the Stack
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def pop_two(values):

Push every value onto an initially empty list-based stack, then pop twice. Return the two popped values as a tuple (first popped, second popped).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values (n >= 2).
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the first popped value, then the second popped value, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def pop_two(values):
    stack = []
    for v in values:
        stack.append(v)
    first = stack.pop()
    second = stack.pop()
    return first, second


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    values = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    first, second = pop_two(values)
    print(first, second)


main()

questions.title: Second From the Top
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def second_from_top(values):

Push every value onto an initially empty list-based stack and return the element just below the top (the second element that would be popped).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values (n >= 2).
Line 2: n integers.

Output Format:
One line with the element second from the top.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000
-1000000 <= value <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def second_from_top(values):
    stack = []
    for v in values:
        stack.append(v)
    top = stack.pop()
    second = stack[-1]
    stack.append(top)
    return second


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    values = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(second_from_top(values))


main()

questions.title: When Is It Warmer?
questions.description:
A weather app tells each day how many days to wait until a strictly warmer day arrives.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def warmer_days(temps):

For each day i, return the number of days until a temperature strictly greater than temps[i] occurs (0 if never).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of days.
Line 2: n integers (the temperatures).

Output Format:
One line with n answers, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-50 <= temperature <= 60
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def warmer_days(temps):
    n = len(temps)
    res = [0] * n
    stack = []
    for i in range(n):
        while stack and temps[stack[-1]] < temps[i]:
            j = stack.pop()
            res[j] = i - j
        stack.append(i)
    return res


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    temps = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, warmer_days(temps))))


main()

questions.title: Stock Price Span Report
questions.description:
A stock dashboard shows, for each day, how many consecutive past days (including today) had a price less than or equal to today's price — the classic stock span.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def stock_spans(prices):

Return the list of spans, one per day, in order. A monotonic stack keeps this O(n).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of days.
Line 2: n integers (the daily prices).

Output Format:
One line with n spans, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= price <= 100000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def read_lines():
    return [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().split('\n') if ln.strip() != '']


def stock_spans(prices):
    n = len(prices)
    spans = [0] * n
    stack = []
    for i in range(n):
        while stack and prices[stack[-1]] <= prices[i]:
            stack.pop()
        spans[i] = i + 1 if not stack else i - stack[-1]
        stack.append(i)
    return spans


def main():
    lines = read_lines()
    prices = list(map(int, lines[1].split()))
    print(' '.join(map(str, stock_spans(prices))))


main()
